title: Signature Drift Attribution Record
description: Signature edition: every detected drift records its attribution — which commit introduced it, whether it was intended, who approved, and what spec change (if any) accompanied it. Drift is never anonymous; the record answers 'who changed the behavior and was it deliberate?' This is a Signature original method.
method: Link each drift to (commit, intent, approver, spec change); query the record during incidents; audit unattributed drifts.
usage: Require attribution on all drift resolutions; audit the unattributed ones first.

demo.code:
print('drift #88: commit a1b2, intended (feature X), approved by lee, spec updated')
print('attribution complete -> closed')

title: Signature Behavioral drift via differential testing
description: Signature edition: Signatures match but behavior drifted: differential testing runs the old and new versions on shared inputs and flags behavioral differences. The detector doesn't judge which behavior is right — it surfaces the drift so humans decide whether the spec or the code needs updating.
method: Run old vs new on a shared corpus; diff outputs; classify differences (intended/unintended); update spec or fix code.
usage: Keep the corpus representative; review every behavioral diff; never silently accept drift.

demo.code:
print('v2.3 vs v2.4 on 10k inputs: 3 outputs differ')
print('triage: 2 intended (changelog), 1 bug -> spec updated, bug fixed')

title: Signature Model-behavior drift (ML)
description: Signature edition: Deployed ML models drift from their validated behavior as data shifts: accuracy decays, calibration worsens, feature distributions move. Drift detectors track prediction distributions, feature drift (PSI/KS tests), and ground-truth accuracy where labels exist — retraining is triggered by measurement, not schedule.
method: Monitor feature distributions and prediction stats; compare to training baseline; retrain on significant drift; validate before swap.
usage: Establish baselines at deploy; monitor continuously; retrain on drift, not on calendar.

demo.code:
print('feature age: PSI 0.31 vs baseline (>0.25 = significant)')
print('DRIFT -> retrain triggered, challenger validated, swapped')

title: Signature Schema evolution compatibility
description: Signature edition: Data schemas (protobuf, Avro, JSON Schema) drift across services: a producer adds a field, a consumer's old schema rejects it. Compatibility checkers (backward/forward/full) verify each schema change against the compatibility policy before it deploys — drift that breaks consumers is caught at the registry, not in production.
method: Register schemas; check each change against the compatibility mode; reject breaking changes; version explicitly.
usage: Enforce compatibility at the registry; version schemas; test consumers against new schemas pre-deploy.

demo.code:
print('schema v7: removed field "name" (BACKWARD mode)')
print('REJECTED: breaks v6 consumers -> use optional field instead')

title: Signature Dependency behavior drift
description: Signature edition: Upgraded dependencies can drift behaviorally while keeping signatures: same function, subtly different results. Detectors run the application's golden tests against dependency upgrades and diff behaviors — the upgrade's behavioral delta is reviewed like a code change.
method: Golden test suite; run against old and new dependency; diff behaviors; review the delta as part of the upgrade PR.
usage: Maintain golden tests for dependency-sensitive behaviors; review every behavioral delta.

demo.code:
print('lib v2.3->v2.4: 2 golden outputs differ (rounding change)')
print('delta reviewed: acceptable -> upgrade approved with note')

title: Signature Spec coverage tracking
description: Signature edition: Drift also means the spec no longer covers the code: new features with no spec, tested behaviors nobody specified. Coverage tracking maps code to spec clauses and reports unspec'd territory — the spec's blind spots, prioritized by risk, scheduled for specification.
method: Map code regions to spec clauses; report unmapped regions; prioritize by risk; schedule spec writing.
usage: Require spec coverage for new features; work down the unspec'd backlog by risk.

demo.code:
print('spec coverage: 78% of code mapped to clauses')
print('unspec\'d: payments/refund.py (HIGH risk) -> spec sprint scheduled')

title: Signature Documentation-code consistency checks
description: Signature edition: Docs drift fastest: examples that no longer run, parameters renamed in code but not docs, architecture diagrams of a system that no longer exists. Consistency checkers extract claims from docs (signatures, examples, diagrams-as-code) and verify each against the code, failing the docs build on mismatch.
method: Extract doc claims; verify against code (signatures, runnable examples, generated diagrams); fail docs build on mismatch.
usage: Generate what can be generated; verify the rest; never let docs build green while wrong.

demo.code:
print('docs claim: f(a, b); code: f(a, b, c=1)')
print('MISMATCH -> docs build FAILED until synced')

title: Signature Contract violation telemetry
description: Signature edition: Contracts deployed as runtime monitors report violations as telemetry: which precondition failed, how often, in what context. A rising violation rate for a previously-stable contract is drift — either callers changed or the contract's assumptions no longer hold in production.
method: Monitor contract checks in production (sampled); track violation rates; alert on trends; investigate whether code or contract drifted.
usage: Sample contract checks in production; dashboard violation trends; investigate sustained increases.

demo.code:
print('contract sorted(a): violations 0.01% -> 2.3% over 2 weeks')
print('DRIFT: new caller passes unsorted data -> contract updated, caller fixed')

title: Signature Test-oracle staleness detection
description: Signature edition: Tests encode the spec; when tests are updated to match new behavior without a spec change, the oracle has drifted. Detectors flag test changes that alter expectations (not just coverage) and require the spec rationale — 'the test changed because the requirement changed' must be stated, not assumed.
method: Diff test expectations across commits; flag expectation changes; require linked requirement/spec updates for each.
usage: Review expectation-changing test edits carefully; they're spec changes in disguise.

demo.code:
print('test_t7: expected 200 -> 404 (expectation changed)')
print('no linked spec change -> BLOCKED: state the requirement or revert')
